learning_outcomes.text: Know electronic measurement systems used in industry.
Know notions of sensors and transducers and their industrial applications.
Know notions of data transmission systems.
Critically discuss results and compare experimental conclusions with theoretical knowledge.
Perform supervised laboratory practices and analyze data taken in practice.
Understand and discuss results obtained in theoretical classes, problem sessions, and the laboratory.
Perform practices and assignments in small groups.
Acquire experience in laboratory work and use advanced electronic equipment.
Become acquainted with the scientific method.
Learn to build a set of design formulas applicable to a given electronic circuit.
Use information sources, both traditional and through new technologies.

syllabus_topics: Systems of order 0, 1st order and 2nd order.
Structure of a data acquisition system.
Practice 1. Development of a temperature meter with Pt100 or another of similar complexity
Practice 2. Development of a liquid conductivity meter, or another of similar complexity.
teaching_methods: Project work (design and construction of measuring instruments)
Practical work (component search, acquisition, instrument construction, adjustment, verification)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.4 * Practices (A) + 0.6 * Exam (B). A minimum grade of 5 points is required in each activity (practices and exam) to pass the course. Approved practice grades are valid only until the extraordinary November session; repeating students must redo practices. Failure to submit practices or attend the exam results in 'no presentado'. More than 30% absence from practice classes leads to a 'no asistente' status for attendance and lab work, which is not recoverable. For extraordinary sessions, all practices must be approved, and the final grade will be based solely on the exam (B), graded up to 10 points. For unique final evaluation, practices must be completed and evaluated, followed by a written exam; both parts must be approved with the same weighting as for ordinary evaluation.
